claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic high-entropy alloy has a typical lamellar as-cast microstructure.
Sub-critical annealing at approximately 650°C for 4–6 hours after solution treatment will form coherent nanoscale precipitates along lamellar interfaces.
The proposed annealing treatment should be conducted in an inert atmosphere.
The specified treatment can produce uniform precipitate development without excessive phase coarsening or decomposition.
The treatment will refine lamellar spacing.
The treatment will strengthen phase boundaries.
The coherent nanoprecipitates impede dislocation motion through Orowan looping.
The precipitate-containing refined microstructure promotes more uniform strain distribution.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength.
More uniform strain distribution delays crack initiation and thereby improves ductility.
Annealing will increase yield strength by approximately 20–30% relative to the untreated as-cast alloy.
Annealing will increase elongation to failure relative to the untreated as-cast alloy.
Annealing will improve fatigue performance relative to the untreated as-cast alloy.
The proposed improvements apply to compositionally similar alloys with lamellar eutectic microstructures produced by conventional casting.
Significant compositional deviations or processing outside the stated conditions may diminish the effect.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies annealing following a solution treatment, whereas the conditions describe treatment of as-cast samples and the experimental design mentions only annealing of the treatment group. It is therefore unclear whether solution treatment is a required step, producing an internally inconsistent test protocol.
